title: Operator Field Autonomy and Observability Contract
author: Asha Menon
content:
Summary:
This contract defines the minimum observability, telemetry, and operator autonomy guarantees for Redwood Private deployments in the field (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for operators, field engineers, solutions engineers, and customer SRE contacts. The goal is to ensure predictable supportability, privacy compliance, and safe operator autonomy while preserving the ability to triage incidents remotely or on-site.

Audience and scope:
- Audience: Field operators, customer SREs, Redwood deployment engineers, security reviewers.
- Scope: All Private mode deployments (VPC and on-prem packaged appliances) delivered after 2025-10-01. Excludes isolated legacy installs with pre-approved exception.

Principles and guarantees:
1) Minimal observability baseline: every installation must export a defined set of metrics, health endpoints, logs, and structured traces to allow Redwood and the customer to validate runtime health and diagnose performance regressions.
2) Operator autonomy: field operators may perform a bounded set of operational actions (start/stop services, rotate local certs, adjust autoscale knobs) defined below. Actions that change cryptographic trust, customer data routing, or model artifacts require coordinated change windows and Redwood approval.
3) Privacy and residency: telemetry must be filtered, sampled, and redacted to meet the customer’s data residency and PII policy. Telemetry that leaves the customer environment must be minimized and tenant-scoped.
4) Fail-safe updates and rollback: all upgrades to telemetry pipelines or observability agents must include canaries, preflight checks, and rollback plans.

Owners and escalation:
- Document owner: eng-private-deployments Observability Squad (primary contact: Asha Menon).
- Field escalation: FieldOps -> SolutionsEng -> Oncall-Redwood-Private -> Security if PII suspected.
- Communication channels: dedicated Slack channel #private-deploy-telemetry, PagerDuty escalation policy: PD-L2 -> PD-L3.

Minimum telemetry contract (table):
Metric/Signal | Unit | Collection frequency | Retention (local) | Export allowed (yes/no) | Purpose
------------- | ---- | -------------------- | ----------------- | ---------------------- | -------
runtime.uptime_seconds | seconds | 10s | 90d | yes | basic liveness and uptime SLO
requests.total | count | 5s | 30d | yes | throughput and capacity planning
latency.p50_ms | ms | 5s | 30d | yes | latency SLO monitoring
kv_cache.hit_ratio | ratio | 30s | 14d | no | local performance tuning (sensitive)
model.load_failures | count | 10s | 90d | yes | model rollout health
disk.free_bytes | bytes | 60s | 14d | yes | storage pressure alerts
auth.failures | count | 10s | 30d | no | security-sensitive, only aggregated metrics exported
logs.system | text | streaming | 14d (rotating) | no except summary | debugging; full logs kept locally
trace.requests | spans | sampled | 7d | yes (sampled) | distributed request tracing

Telemetry collection config (examples):
- Prometheus scrape config (field appliance):
  - job_name: redwood-runtime
    metrics_path: /metrics
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['127.0.0.1:9090']
    relabel_configs:
      - source_labels: ['__address__']
        target_label: 'instance'
- Fluent Bit snapshot config (logs -> local buffer):
  [SERVICE]
    Flush 5
    Log_Level info
  [INPUT]
    Name tail
    Path /var/log/redwood/runtime/*.log
    Tag runtime.*
  [FILTER]
    Name grep
    Match runtime.*
    Regex message (?!.*(SSN|credit_card))
  [OUTPUT]
    Name file
    Match *
    Path /var/lib/redwood/logs/forwarded/%Y-%m-%d.log

Sampling and export policy:
- Default metric export: full for non-PII numerical metrics.
- Log export: only pre-aggregated summaries or alerts may be exported offsite. Raw logs containing potentially sensitive values must remain on local storage and be retrievable under traceable support request with customer consent.
- Trace sampling: default 0.5% global; 100% for error traces (status >= 500) for 30 minutes after an incident detection window.
- Snapshot window: when a critical incident is declared, operators may trigger a 15-minute high-resolution capture (metrics at 1s, traces full, logs forwarded) — requires email or Slack approval from customer contact unless pre-authorized in the contract.

Data handling and privacy safeguards:
- Redaction rules: all log lines MUST be run through the redaction filter that removes email addresses, credit card numbers, and Social Security/ID patterns.
- Local encryption: telemetry at rest must be encrypted using the host KMS (LUKS or cloud KMS-backed) with keys managed by the customer where supported.
- Egress controls: allowlist IPs for telemetry export must be established during onboarding. Any change to allowlist requires a signed change order.
- Data residency: export endpoints must be in the customer-approved region. Global export of tenant-level data is disallowed by default.

Operator autonomy matrix (what field ops can do without Redwood):
- Can: restart runtime services (redwood-runtime.service), clear local non-persistent caches, rotate TLS certs using pre-shared CSR procedure, adjust local autoscaler thresholds within vendor-defined safe ranges, collect local diagnostics bundle.
- Cannot (without coordinated change): replace model artifact repositories, change outbound telemetry allowlist, change KMS key bindings, modify control plane endpoint URLs, adjust privilege escalation or RBAC policies.

Deployment acceptance checklist (numbered):
1) Confirm hardware inventory matches Customer Requirements Minimums and serial numbers registered.
2) Confirm network ACLs and egress allowlist are as documented.
3) Verify Prometheus and Fluent Bit are running and serving /metrics and /health endpoints.
4) Run preflight acceptance tests (see validation queries).
5) Verify telemetry export endpoints are reachable and export handshake succeeds (TLS verification).
6) Validate local encryption at rest and KMS integration.
7) Create and upload initial support bundle to customer-controlled storage; validate retrieval.

Validation queries (examples):
- Prometheus: up{job="redwood-runtime"} == 1
- Alert query: increase(runtime.uptime_seconds[5m]) > 0
- Log sample: grep -E "ERROR|WARN" /var/lib/redwood/logs/recent.log | tail -n 50
- KV cache sanity: curl -s localhost:9091/debug/kv_status | jq '.entries | length'

Upgrade and rollback procedure for observability agents:
1) Author preflight: publish agent version and change log to deployment ticket.
2) Canary: roll to 5% of hosts (or 1 host in single-node installs) and monitor for 30 minutes for: CPU spikes (>20% baseline), missing metrics, or log volume anomalies.
3) Automated tests: run scrape verification and sample trace exports.
4) Gradual roll: 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 15 minute observation windows.
5) Rollback: if any canary fails, trigger immediate rollback to previous agent image and collect support bundle with failing host telemetry.
Commands (examples):
- Verify metrics endpoint: curl -fsS http://localhost:9090/metrics | head -n 20
- Collect support bundle: sudo /opt/redwood/bin/collect-support-bundle --out /tmp/bundle.tar.gz --since 1h
- Rollback agent: sudo dpkg -i /var/cache/redwood/agent-1.2.3.deb || sudo apt-get install --reinstall redwood-agent=1.2.2

Operational playbooks (short):
- High CPU/latency during model load:
  1. Check model.load_failures and runtime memory pressure.
  2. If KV cache thrash detected, clear non-persistent cache and schedule model reload with reduced batch size.
  3. If persistent, open ticket with Redwood runtime team and attach support bundle.
- Telemetry export blocked (network):
  1. Verify egress ACLs and DNS resolution.
  2. If outbound is blocked, set local retention to high-resolution buffer; mark incident and schedule assisted export under customer approval.

Acceptance tests and SLOs for observability pipeline:
- Metric availability SLO: 99.9% of expected metric series should be present in Prometheus for each 24h window.
- Alerting latency SLO: critical alerts (node down, model load failure) must generate notification within 30s of detection.
- Support bundle retrieval SLO: support bundle generated and retrievable within 10 minutes of request during business hours.

Templates and example artifacts (appendix):
- Support bundle contents: /var/lib/redwood/logs/*, /etc/redwood/config.yaml, /opt/redwood/state/kv_snapshot.json, prometheus-scrape-logs, system journal tail.
- Example redaction regex: (?: \d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4} )|(?: 4[0-9]{12}(?:[0-9]{3})? )|(?:[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,})
